text:
liam: quick q — planning to land an optional request param `score_adjust` on POST /v1/rerank to tweak final scores. if we add this, do older clients see any change in ordering? trying to avoid surprises for canary users

sara: short answer: older clients won't send the field so they won't be affected client-side, but server-side tie-break logic will change if we start applying `score_adjust` for all requests. we need a clear backcompat guarantee: default behavior for requests without the field must be unchanged. :ok_hand:

anika: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank/pull/642 — adds optional score_adjust and returns score_meta.adjusted_score. here's the example request shape i'm proposing:

```json
{
  "query": "best pizza near me",
  "candidates": ["loc_123", "loc_456", "loc_789"],
  "score_adjust": 0.12  // optional float, applied after model score
}
```

jdoe: couple notes: 1) keep `score` as the original model score for backcompat (unchanged numeric semantics). 2) add `score_meta.adjusted_score` (nullable) and `score_meta.rank_seed` so downstream can reproduce ordering. 3) update OpenAPI and client generator mapping.

mike: concern: what happens if model returns `null` or `NaN` for a candidate score? we currently fallback to original input order + stable sort. if we introduce adjusted_score step we must preserve deterministic fallback for missing values. also need to define behavior for equal floats (ties) — existing stable-sort uses candidate index which is fine but breaks reproducibility if request includes nondeterministic candidate order.

yasmin: propose explicit tie-breaker algorithm to put in the contract:
1) If both adjusted_score present: compare adjusted_score (desc).
2) Else if at least one adjusted_score present: treat missing as -inf (so present always wins).
3) If adjusted_score equal or absent: compare `score` (desc).
4) If still equal or both null: use `score_meta.rank_hint` if provided (higher wins).
5) Final deterministic fallback: stable hash(candidate_id + request.rerank_id) (desc).

this guarantees deterministic ordering even for older clients (they just won't send score_adjust or rerank_id).

liam: that sounds good. two followups: a) can we avoid exposing hash in responses (keep internal only)? b) should `score_meta.rank_hint` be suggested by model adapters or only by reranker logic?

sara: a) yes keep hash internal (don't expose). b) `rank_hint` optional, models/adapters may populate it to carry learned tie-break signals (e.g., recency). if absent, fallback holds. i'll add a migration note that `score` remains canonical for clients that don't read `score_meta`. :memo:

anika: will add unit tests for NaN/null and equal-value scenarios + an integration canary that compares ordering before/after the change with a small traffic slice. pinging @deploy-bot for scheduled canary.

deploy-bot: Canary job scheduled: `rerank-contract-canary` — start=2024-11-02T03:00:00Z, duration=2h, percent=1% :rocket:

jdoe: also adding small compatibility test in the client-gen CI that validates generated SDKs still parse `score` as number and ignore unknown fields (per JSON-Schema additionalProperties=true).

mike: one nit — document explicitly that servers MUST NOT mutate `score` in-place when `score_adjust` is present; always write adjusted result into `score_meta.adjusted_score` and keep `score` untouched. this keeps telemetry consistent.

yasmin: agreed. i'll draft the OpenAPI diff and the contract text for the tie-breaker and post in the PR.

liam: awesome, thanks everyone. sara/anika — once PR is green can we get a short changelog blurb for releases and a note in the Console schema migration page? i'll loop product if there are UX implications. :+1:
